newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ZOLA DOES NOT RULE OUT MOVE TO ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZOLA DOES NOT RULE OUT MOVE TO ENGLAND.

text.p: Parma midfielder Gianfranco Zola, commenting on media reports of an imminent move to Chelsea, said on Wednesday that he had problems with his Italian club but denied he had been in contact with English teams.
However, he did not rule out a move.

"I have problems with Parma but I hope to resolve them," the 30-year-old Sardinian told Reuters on the plane bringing the Italian national team back from Sarajevo, where they were surprisingly beaten 2-1 by Bosnia earlier in the day.
"If I can't resolve them then who knows?"

The daily Corriere dello Sport earlier reported, under a headline "Zola is leaving", that Chelsea had offered 13 billion lire ($7.8 million) to secure the player alongside Italian internationals Roberto Di Matteo and Gianluca Vialli.
It added, however, that other premier league clubs -- Manchester United, Newcastle and Tottenham -- were also after Zola.
Zola, who has played 102 league games for Parma and scored 49 goals, has had disagreements with new coach Carlo Ancelotti over where he should play in the team.
Ancelotti reportedly wants him in a right-midfield role which Zola dislikes and does not feel comfortable with.
"I know that other clubs are interested in me," Zola said. "But I don't know anything about Chelsea. This story has come from the club. I have spoken to nobody about this."
Asked whether he would like to play in English soccer, Zola replied: "That is another story. It is not something that I really want to discuss at this stage."
